claim: UFO tart origin (1955 Hainanese baker Fu Ah On, accidental over-baking), price ~RM2.50, kopitiams that sell it, and Sabah's 5 May 'UFO Tart Day'.
quote: The born of UFO Tart is simply an accident happened over 60 years ago... Kedai Kopi Wing Hup Lee, Syn Ming Hing, San Da Gen Kopitiam. 5 May is declared as the 'UFO Tart Day' of Sabah.

claim: UFO tart description and San Da Gen location; English Tea House scone/tea; Yap Syn Kee grass jelly; Ngee Lee coconut pudding in a shell.
quote: a thin butter sponge cake base topped with a smooth, eggy custard and finished with a piping of fluffy meringue ... Made from coconut milk rather than coconut water, it's served in an actual coconut.

claim: Sim Sim Water Village eating: Bridges 7 and 8, Kau Kee G68 spring noodle and century-egg dumpling (sells out before 10am), Sim-Sim 88 seafood hours, no-MSG claim.
quote: The famous dining area is on 7th and 8th bridge... Kau Kee (九记) at G68... Spring Noodle... Century Egg Dumpling... They don't even need to use MSG.

claim: English Tea House sits in restored colonial Newlands beside Agnes Newton Keith's home, with sprawling lawns over Sandakan Bay; fine-dining western cuisine.
quote: served as home to American writer Agnes Newton Keith, author of 'Land Below The Wind' (1939) ... 'sprawling green lawns' and commanding views overlooking Sandakan Bay and the Sulu Sea.

claim: The Nest at Sepilok Forest Edge: Bornean Contemporary cuisine, signature dishes and prices (asam pedas oxtail RM63, hinava RM36, lamb curry RM48, nasi lemak burger RM31), 7am-10pm.
quote: Bornean Contemporary Cuisine ... Asam Pedas Oxtail (63) — Special signature by our Chef ... Hinava — raw fish with shallots, ginger, chilies, lime (36).

claim: Sandakan became the 'Little Hong Kong' of Sabah by the 1930s via pre-WWII Cantonese merchant immigration.
quote: Sandakan became the 'Little Hong Kong' of Sabah by the 1930s due to waves of pre-World War II immigration that brought more Cantonese merchants to the city.

claim: Hainanese founded Sandakan's kopitiam culture; Hakka is the Chinese community's internal lingua franca; Sabah Chinese food blends Hakka/Cantonese/Hokkien.
quote: Hainanese coffeehouse operators established the kopi tiam culture that persists today ... The Hakka dialect functions as the Chinese community's internal lingua franca.

claim: Sandakan spring noodles (Hong Kong diaspora, 'rubber noodles') and fish-paste noodles served clear/curry/prawn or Hakka style with minced pork.
quote: Sandakan, Sabah's second-largest city, was once known as 'Little Hong Kong' ... They take their fish seriously here ... Hakka style, where minced pork is liberally added to the fish-heavy mix.

claim: Persatuan Perikanan (fishermen's association) no-menu seafood feast; sang har mee at Empire; Ba Lin rooftop sea view; Kafeteria/Sepilok eats.
quote: Serving only the freshest seafood available on the day, all you need to do is to say 'yes' to all of them.

claim: Detailed Sandakan food trail with stalls/kopitiams, addresses and specialties (Central Market kueh teow stall, Kong Teck, Wing Hup Lee, Persatuan Perikanan, Pasar Kim Fung).
quote: Sandakan Central Market ... 'The original kueh Teow with deep-fried pork' (Stall 33) ... Persatuan Perikanan Sandakan ... No-menu restaurant; freshest daily seafood catch (4 tables only—reserve ahead).

claim: Daily food budget RM30-50; night-market meals under RM15; seafood bak kut teh at Nam Chai; ngiu chap; latok sea grapes; salted-fish fried rice.
quote: RM30–RM50/day covers a full day of meals including snacks and drinks ... Sabahan Ngiu Chap ... a dish that locals swear cures hangovers, bad days, and rainy mornings.

claim: 15 famous Sandakan dishes incl. hinava (Kadazan-Dusun raw fish), ikan/lokan bakar, kam heong & butter prawns at Empire/Ocean King, kolo mee.
quote: Hinava ... slices of fresh raw fish marinated in lime juice, chili, ginger, and shallots ... Lokan Bakar ... grilled over charcoal.

claim: Sim Sim seafood (chef Ah Kit, salted fish), Nam Chai peppery seafood bak kut teh, Gold Crown UFO tart, Empire prawn noodles.
quote: chef Ah Kit 'insists on only cooking with the freshest seafood' ... Nam Chai ... broth 'more peppery than those serving Kuala Lumpur'.

claim: Sang nyuk mian definition (Hakka 'raw pork noodle', pork cooked in cloudy broth, served kon lau or soup); Moon n Star among Sandakan's best.
quote: Sang nyuk mian means 'raw pork noodles' in Hakka, but the thinly sliced pork is cooked in a signature cloudy broth before being served with noodles.

claim: UFO tart is a genuine ~70-year Sabah heritage snack now exported (kaya/matcha flavours sold in Singapore).
quote: Sabah Sandakan UFO Tart – Malaysian Heritage Snack With Kaya and Matcha Flavours.

claim: Sim Sim Seafood Restaurant praised for Sandakan-style ikan bakar (grilled fish half-fried then charcoal-grilled to order).
quote: Sandakan style Ikan Bakar (Grilled fish) ... fish already half fried and grilled when an order is made.

claim: Buli Sim Sim is the original townsite of Sandakan (founded 1879), hundreds of wooden stilt houses on the sea, reachable by plank walkways.
quote: Kampung Buli Sim Sim ... is the site of the original town of Sandakan which began in 1879 ... built by hundreds of wooden stilt houses on the sea.

claim: Waterfront Seafood Bar & Grill at Harbour Mall: open-air dining right by the sea, fresh seafood, white clams and butter prawns.
quote: a culinary gem situated in a breathtaking location right by the sea ... renowned for its fresh seafood offerings and inviting open-air atmosphere.

claim: Waterfront Seafood reviews highlight white clams, dry butter prawns, generous portions and reasonable prices.
quote: Guests rave about the delicious dishes like white clams and dry butter prawns, all served in generous portions at reasonable prices.

claim: Ocean King Seafood (Batu Sapi): open-air floor over the water with live tanks to pick your own; ranked #5; pricier, value mixed.
quote: a very large open air floor set over the water with tanks holding live seafood, and you can go and select your own dinner.

claim: Ocean King sources seafood locally and serves traditional Chinese seafood preparations.
quote: renowned for its fresh seafood offerings and traditional Chinese cuisine, sourcing its seafood directly from local waters.

claim: English Tea House reviews: loved for view, lawn and atmosphere; food quality mixed (some inconsistencies noted).
quote: much loved restaurant for locals and a popular tourist destination with its great food, excellent service and beautiful views ... some reviewers note inconsistencies in food quality.

claim: Ba Lin Roof Garden is Sandakan's only rooftop garden bar-bistro atop NAK Hotel, western menu, bay views.
quote: The Coolest (only) rooftop garden bar & bistro in Sandakan.

claim: Kim Fung Night Market: Saturday only 5-10pm, ~6.5km from centre, hundreds of stalls of Chinese and halal street food, lion/fish dance from 8pm, authentic non-touristy.
quote: a wide variety of Chinese and Halal (Muslim) street food are sold there ... an authentic local market that shows the colors and diversity of our society.

claim: Sandakan earned the 'Little Hong Kong' nickname 1920s-1950s for its thriving Chinese merchant community and shophouse architecture.
quote: Sandakan earned the 'Little Hong Kong' nickname through the 1920s–1950s because of its thriving Chinese merchant community ... dense shophouse architecture.

claim: Sepilok Jungle Resort (Banana Cafe) is at Jalan Rambutan, Sepilok Mile 14, near the orangutan sanctuary.
quote: Sepilok Jungle Resort is located at Jalan Rambutan, Sepilok Mile 14, Sandakan, Sabah, Malaysia.

claim: Kafeteria Sepilok, steps from the Orangutan Centre: sandwiches from RM6, rice/noodles from RM8, cold coffee RM2.80, daily 8-4, cash only.
quote: It serves sandwiches from six ringgit and noodles and rice dishes from eight ringgit ... open daily 08:00-16:00 and cash only.

claim: Sepilok dining is very limited and pricey; Sepilok Nature Lodge restaurant ~RM98 for two with beer, western-leaning; Banana Cafe weak.
quote: in Sepilok your eating venues are severely limited ... RM98 for a meal for two (with beer) ... wine reaches RM160 per bottle.

claim: The Nest has the most interesting menu in the whole Sandakan area; Kafeteria Sepilok and Banana Cafe are the budget local options near the sanctuary.
quote: The Nest ... offers the most interesting menu in Sepilok, or in fact in the whole Sandakan area.

claim: Sepilok Nature Resort: cooked-to-order breakfast, all-day deli, east-west fusion served on a terrace over the lodge lake/forest.
quote: meals combining flavours from both east and west can be enjoyed on the terrace of the lodge's restaurant.

claim: Kinabatangan river lodges serve included, locally-sourced buffet meals; barefoot dining with sarongs and riverside tables at some lodges.
quote: everyone must be bare-foot in the dining area ... buffet meals for breakfast, lunch and dinner and a selection of local beers and wines.

claim: Sabah Traditional Cooking Class (Papar): market tour plus family-home cooking of rendang/likku with 'Mummy Halimah', min 2, book a day ahead.
quote: Your adventure begins with a local market tour, where you'll handpick fresh ingredients ... guided by Mummy Halimah.

claim: TYH Borneo Tours offers a Sabahan cooking class experience that can be arranged on request.
quote: Cooking Class

claim: The Sea Garden Sim-sim is a waterside seafood dining option in the Harbour Mall Sandakan orbit.
quote: The Sea Garden Sim-sim

claim: Sepilok dining trio: The Lake Bistro (Malay+international, lake views), Banana Cafe (simple jungle fare), The Nest (burgers/wraps/curries, beautiful at night) — Nest often has items missing.
quote: The Nest did always seem to have a couple of items missing off the menu ... The Lake Bistro and Bar serves a mix of traditional Malay and international cuisine.

claim: Sandakan food trail: Central Market kueh teow stall since 1940 (one item only), Kong Teck fish noodles, Sim Sim Bridge 7 rubber wantan noodles, Nam Chai seafood bak kut teh, Bun Hock UFO tarts.
quote: Original Homemade Kueh Teow with Deep-fried Pork ... Established since 1940; serves only this one item.

claim: Sanda'Gen Downtown Night Market sits on the seawall at Coastal Road (Tembok Bandar Sandakan) with about 36 food stalls.
quote: It features around thirty-six food stalls offering an array of delectable treats.
